records.title: baseline
records.statement: Pin the accepted C++ language dialect, compiler and standard library version, build flags, and ABI environment needed to reproduce in-scope upstream behavior.

records.title: ownership
records.statement: Verify transfer, sharing, and non-owning alias guarantees at supported C++ object interfaces before substituting Rust ownership.

records.title: lifetime
records.statement: Verify reference and pointer validity, temporary lifetime extension, and observable invalidation at supported C++ object boundaries.

records.title: raii
records.statement: Verify required RAII resource release, destructor side effects, and observable destruction order during normal exits.

records.title: copy
records.statement: Verify observable C++ copy-construction and copy-assignment semantics, including ownership and independence of copied state.

records.title: move
records.statement: Verify required move-construction and move-assignment results, including documented moved-from guarantees, without assuming every moved-from value is empty.

records.title: exceptions
records.statement: Verify externally observable C++ exception types, propagation, and the approved translation to Rust errors at compatible interfaces.

records.title: unwind
records.statement: Verify required cleanup and object destruction during exception unwinding and equivalent Rust failure paths.

records.title: noexcept
records.statement: Where noexcept or termination behavior is externally contractual, verify no-throw boundaries and required termination outcomes without allowing exceptions across unsupported FFI.

records.title: templates
records.statement: Verify consumed C++ template instantiation and constraint acceptance/rejection behavior for supported source/API combinations.

records.title: overloads
records.statement: Verify accepted overload selection and implicit conversion effects at externally consumed C++ APIs.

records.title: value categories
records.statement: Verify relevant C++ value-category and forwarding behavior when it changes supported public API results or ownership transitions.

records.title: virtual dispatch
records.statement: Verify observable virtual override dispatch and inheritance behavior of supported polymorphic interfaces.

records.title: rtti
records.statement: Verify public RTTI and checked downcast behavior where consumers depend on dynamic_cast, typeid, or equivalent type discovery.

records.title: object layout
records.statement: Where native object representations cross a binary boundary, verify relevant field layout, size, alignment and permitted representation assumptions against the pinned C++ ABI.

records.title: binary abi
records.statement: Verify required calling conventions, exposed binary symbols, and toolchain-specific name-mangling compatibility across retained C++/Rust binary interfaces.

records.title: cross language allocation
records.statement: Verify allocation and deallocation ownership, exception barriers and object lifetime across necessary C++/Rust interop boundaries.

records.title: container invalidation
records.statement: Where consumers rely on C++ container/iterator contracts, verify invalidation, iteration and reference-stability behavior at exposed boundaries.

records.title: atomics
records.statement: Verify required atomic modification ordering, acquire/release visibility, and synchronization guarantees for in-scope concurrent behavior; do not compare unpromised scheduling order.

records.title: thread sync
records.statement: Verify accepted mutex, lock, condition-variable, and wakeup/predicate behavior for supported multithreaded interactions.

records.title: static lifecycle
records.statement: Verify observable initialization and teardown ordering for supported static and thread-local objects when it affects externally visible behavior.

records.title: coroutines
records.statement: Where C++20 coroutines are part of the accepted upstream interface, verify resume, suspend, cancellation and destruction contracts in the Rust replacement.

records.title: defined behavior
records.statement: Distinguish specified C++ behavior from undefined, implementation-defined and unspecified behavior when setting compatibility acceptance; document environment-specific decisions rather than asserting impossible universal parity.

records.title: numeric
records.statement: Verify supported C++ integer promotions, conversion widths, signedness, floating-point and rounding outcomes wherever consumers observe them.
